content.title: About
content.content: Canned asparagus consists of cooked asparagus spears packed in a jar with added fat to enhance flavor and preserve texture. The product is ready to eat and is commonly used in salads, side dishes, and hot meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Asparagus has been cultivated since ancient Rome and is one of the first spring vegetables.
Canning allows the vegetable to retain its nutrients for up to three years when stored properly.
Adding fat (usually a vegetable oil) improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin K.
Canned asparagus jars are often identified with the USDA code “4598”.
Heat processing enhances aromatic compounds that give asparagus its distinctive flavor.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains folate
items.content: Folate supports DNA synthesis and is especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Asparagus provides glutathione and vitamin C, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: One cup of canned asparagus contains about 25 kcal, making it a diet‑friendly choice.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Canned vegetables often contain added salt; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Allergy to added oil
items.content: If a specific vegetable oil is used, individuals with oil sensitivities may react.

items.title: Bacterial risk from compromised cans
items.content: Bulging or damaged cans can harbor harmful bacteria and should be discarded.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned asparagus can be eaten cold in salads, warmed in the microwave, or added to soups and stews. If desired, drain excess fat and drizzle with olive oil for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer the contents to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3‑4 days.
